title: How do we write a quantity in decimal form?
description: Four quantities named by their places are written as decimals and read aloud. An empty place is held by a zero. Keeko's doubt is that the zero can be left out of four ones and six hundredths.
teaching_notes: One idea: put each digit in its own place and fill every empty place with a zero. Watch for students who write four point six for four ones and six hundredths.

source: Write each quantity in decimal form, with its place values, and read it: (a) 2 ones, 3 tenths and 5 hundredths (b) 1 ten and 5 tenths (c) 4 ones and 6 hundredths (d) 1 hundred, 1 one and 1 hundredth.
video_script.why: The child has written the digits 7, 0 and 5 in different places and now writes quantities given by their places.
video_script.substitution: Each part goes in its own place after or before the point, and a zero holds every empty place.
video_script.anchor: a place value chart with hundreds, tens, units, a point, tenths and hundredths
video_script.wrong_move: leaves out the zero that holds the empty tenths place
video_script.payoff_line: Every empty place is filled with a zero

final_answer.spoken: two point three five, ten point five, four point zero six and one hundred one point zero one

video_script.fraction_reading: tenths and hundredths are said as words
maths_rules: (c) 4 + 0/10 + 6/100 = 4.06, a zero holds the empty tenths place, read four point zero six
(d) 100 + 0 + 1 + 0/10 + 1/100 = 101.01, read one hundred one point zero one
the slip: 4.6 is 4 + 6/10, which is not 4 + 6/100
video_script.design: The place value chart stays on the stage; each quantity drops its digits into the chart in the working band, with a zero appearing in each empty place. Keeko's doubt compares four point six with four point zero six.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book, then the four quantities (a) 2 ones, 3 tenths and 5 hundredths (b) 1 ten and 5 tenths (c) 4 ones and 6 hundredths (d) 1 hundred, 1 one and 1 hundredth; a question mark in the anchor band
narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about writing quantities as decimals.
<bookmark mark='list'/>Four quantities are given in words, like two ones and three tenths.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Write each one in decimal form, with its place values, and read it aloud.

beats.on_screen: the quantities stay on the board; Keeko sits beside them as the child
narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a place value chart: hundreds, tens, units, a point, tenths and hundredths

marks.chart: the chart of places is drawn
marks.zero: a zero appears in a blank place

narration: <bookmark mark='chart'/>Here is the place value chart, with a point after the units.
<bookmark mark='zero'/>Every place must hold a digit, so an empty place is filled with a zero.

beats.on_screen: Given: four quantities named by their places
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, four quantities named by their places.

beats.on_screen: To find: each quantity in decimal form, and how to read it
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to write each quantity in decimal form and read it aloud.

beats.on_screen: Step 1 (a): 2 + 3/10 + 5/100 = 2.35, read two point three five

marks.a: 2, 3 and 5 drop into units, tenths and hundredths

narration: <bookmark mark='a'/>Step one, put two ones, three tenths and five hundredths in their places.
<bookmark mark='write'/>We write it as two point three five, and we read it the same way.

marks.b: 1 drops into tens and 5 into tenths
marks.write: 10.5 is written with a zero in the units place

narration: <bookmark mark='b'/>Step two, one ten and five tenths make ten plus five tenths.
<bookmark mark='write'/>That is written ten point five, with a zero holding the empty units place.

beats.on_screen: Step 3 (c): 4 + 0/10 + 6/100 = 4.06, with a zero in the empty tenths place, read four point zero six

marks.c: 4 drops into units and 6 into hundredths
marks.zero: a zero fills the tenths place, and 4.06 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='c'/>Step three, four ones and six hundredths have no tenths.
<bookmark mark='zero'/>The tenths place is empty, so we put a zero there and write four point zero six.

beats.on_screen: Step 4 (d): 100 + 0 + 1 + 0/10 + 1/100 = 101.01, read one hundred one point zero one

marks.d: 1, 1 and 1 drop into hundreds, units and hundredths
marks.zero: zeros fill the tens and tenths, and 101.01 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='d'/>Step four, one hundred, one unit and one hundredth leave two places empty.
<bookmark mark='zero'/>Zeros fill the tens and the tenths, and we write one hundred one point zero one.

marks.first: the first two answers are marked
marks.last: the last two answers are marked

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Every empty place is filled with a zero.
<bookmark mark='first'/>The first two numbers are two point three five and ten point five.
<bookmark mark='last'/>The last two are four point zero six and one hundred one point zero one.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the place value chart
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: 4.6 appears and is struck out; the chart shows 6 in hundredths with a zero in tenths; 4.06 is written

marks.doubt: 4.6 appears with the 6 in the tenths place
marks.fix: the 6 moves to hundredths and a zero fills the tenths place

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks four ones and six hundredths is four point six, because the six comes next.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But the six is hundredths, not tenths. The empty tenths place needs a zero, so the number is four point zero six.
